atomic_operand_register.claim: The RMW operand register of atomic_mem / atomic_rmw IS encoded in the instruction, in byte+5 bit 7 and byte+6 bits 0..5, as an index into the operand register window. db.json states it 'is implicit (supplied by the preceding op / amode)' and DOC-02 section 3 row 9 ranks it a MISSING field -- 'the worst kind of gap for an emitter'.
atomic_operand_register.conflicts_with: db.json/validation.json call byte+5 `index_reg` ('per-lane index GPR, zeroed for a uniform address') and byte+6 `addr_desc` ('framing only'). Our atdevimm carrier uses a UNIFORM address yet the compiler emits byte+5/+6 = 0x80/0x02, which the per-lane reading does not explain. The address role is not excluded for the per-lane form; the DATA role is now proven for the uniform form.
atomic_operand_register.corollary: The redirected register is CONSUMED -- its later reader gets 0 -- which is the same register-release contract EXP-0086/0089/0099 document for the ALU families.
atomic_operand_register.evidence: Carrier kernels/atomic_dev.metal keeps a[0..3] = 7/1007/2007/3007 live across atomic_fetch_add(o, a[0]). Baseline byte+5/+6 = 0x00/0x00 -> the counter is 7. byte+5 = 0x80 -> the counter is 1007 AND the later store of a[1]'s register reads 0. byte+6 = 0x01 (also 0x41/0x81/0xC1, so bits 6-7 are don't-care) -> the counter is 2007 AND a[2]'s later reader reads 0. Identical in both gated runs.
atomic_operand_register.model: operand_register_index = (byte+5 >> 7) | ((byte+6 & 0x3F) << 1), relative to the register the compiler's own encoding selects. PROVEN AT ALL FOUR CONSTRUCTIBLE INDICES: 0 -> a[0] = 7, 1 -> a[1] = 1007, 2 -> a[2] = 2007, and -- built for the first time by addendum arm `atdev_operand_pair` (byte+5 pinned 0x80, byte+6 swept densely) -- 3 -> a[3] = 3007, each with the redirected register's later reader zeroed. byte+6 bits 6 and 7 are DON'T CARE (0x01/0x41/0x81/0xC1 all give index 3). The `<< 1` multiplier is no longer interpolated.
atomic_operand_register.residual_unknown: With byte+5 = 0x80, byte+6 values 0x30 and 0x31 restore the BASELINE operand instead of selecting index 97/99, and they are the only two cases in the addendum whose acceptance disagreed between run21 and run22. Unexplained; recorded.

device_load_addr_mode_not_an_enum.caveat: Only the terminal scalar 32-bit shape was tested. The enum may still select behaviour for the base-sharing / CF / RT forms it names.
device_load_addr_mode_not_an_enum.claim: device_load byte+2 (`addr_mode`) is INERT for a terminal scalar 32-bit indexed load: all 256 values load correctly, including every code in db.json's enum.

device_load_dst_fields.claim: device_load.dst_lo and dst_ext9 carry NO register information. dst_lo must be exactly 1; only bit 0 of dst_ext9 is live and must be 1. Three constrained bits out of the nine the two fields span; the other six are don't-care.
device_load_dst_fields.evidence: 4/4 dst_lo values and 128/128 dst_ext9 values swept at four independent target registers (3, 7, 20, 33), plus the full 512-value 2-D product at r7. The accepted set is identical at every target register.
device_load_dst_fields.supersedes: EXP-M4-13's dst = dst_lo | (dst_ext9 << 2) (already retracted by EXP-0101) and EXP-0101's own operational advice to copy the pair verbatim per addr_mode/ld_format shape. The pair is a fixed 3-bit enable pattern, not a per-shape token.

device_store_addr_mode_bit1_is_context_d.claim: device_store byte+2 bit 1 selects the DATA SOURCE: clear = ALU-computed, set = direct live load-result. It is inert when the data is ALU-computed (256/256 pass), which is the configuration EXP-0119 measured and reported as 'INERT here'; with a load-forwarded source only the 128 bit1-set values work and the other 128 store 0.

reserved_fields_that_are_not_reserved.claim: atomic_mem.rsv10 (4 of 256 values work), atomic_mem.rsv11 (1 of 256), atomic_tg.rsv4 (4 of 256), atomic_tg.rsv6 (2 of 256) and atomic_tg.rsv9 (1 of 256) are LIVE, heavily constrained bytes, not reserved padding. device_load.reserved7/reserved13 and device_store.reserved7/reserved13 ARE genuinely inert (256/256 each).

device_load.dst_ext9.semantics: BIT 0 must be 1 -- all 64 odd values work and all 64 even values silently zero, identically at target registers 3, 7, 20 and 33. Not a register extension of any kind. How many of bits 1..6 are additionally free is ld_format-DEPENDENT (addendum H8, 21 formats x the full 512-value product): for 16 of the 21 accepted formats the rule is `v & 0x181 == 0x081` (bits 1..6 all free); for ld_format 3/7/9/13 it is `v & 0x1C1 == 0x081` (bit 6 must also be 0); for ld_format 39 it is `v & 0x1E1 == 0x081` (bits 5 and 6 must be 0). `dst_ext9 = 1` satisfies ALL 21.

It is live exactly when the stored data is a live load result. Both halves swept densely in both source shapes.
device_store.addr_mode.semantics: DATA-SOURCE SELECTOR, and it is bit 1: with an ALU-computed source all 256 values work, but with a DIRECT load-result source only the 128 values with bit1 SET work (0x56-class), and the 128 with bit1 clear (0x54-class) store 0.

device_store.elem_size.label: hardware-run
device_store.elem_size.note: Extends EXP-0082's 25 probed store-side values to the full byte.
device_store.elem_size.semantics: 96 of 256 raw byte+12 values store correctly.

device_store.extmode.label: hardware-run
device_store.extmode.note: The 0xC0 alternative is now characterised rather than merely observed. Its MEANING is still unknown; only that it is accepted.
device_store.extmode.semantics: SOURCE REGISTER SELECTOR: exactly TWO values work for a source register R, namely `2*R` and `2*R | 0xC0`. Proven by moving the source register and re-sweeping densely (addendum H10): r4 -> {8, 200}, r8 -> {16, 208}, r12 -> {24, 216}. So `extmode >> 1` is the source register (EXP-0090's formula, now dense over three registers), bit 0 is LIVE here unlike device_load.extmode, and bits 6+7 TOGETHER are an accepted alternative form -- a modifier, not register bits (neither bit alone works).

device_store.reserved13.label: hardware-run
device_store.reserved13.semantics: INERT. All 256 values leave the store correct.

device_store.reserved7.label: hardware-run
device_store.reserved7.semantics: INERT. All 256 values leave the store correct.

device_store.space.label: hardware-run
device_store.space.semantics: Exact rule `v & 0x02 == 0x00`: bit 1 is live and must be 0 for a device-space store; bit 0 and bits 2..7 are DON'T CARE (128 of 256 values work).

device_store.st_desc_hi.label: hardware-run
device_store.st_desc_hi.semantics: byte+11 bits 2..7. Machine-derived exact rule `v & 0x11 == 0x00`: bits 0 AND 4 of the field are live and must be 0; bits 1..3 and 5 are DON'T CARE (16 of 64 values work).

device_store.st_format.label: hardware-run
device_store.st_format.note: First execution of synthesised store-format codes; EXP-M4-13 was compile-only.
device_store.st_format.semantics: Store data-format descriptor. 84 of 256 values store the 32-bit scalar correctly, the same 84 with an ALU-computed and with a load-forwarded source.

device_store.st_format_ext.label: hardware-run
device_store.st_format_ext.note: Was `corpus-correlation` ('bit set only for the 3-component store').
device_store.st_format_ext.semantics: Only the low 5 bits are free: exactly 0..31 work, 32..127 break the store, so bits 5 and 6 of the field are live and must be 0.

mem_fence.b5.label: corpus-correlation
mem_fence.b5.semantics: INERT with respect to the carrier's output: all 256 values pass.

mem_fence.memclass.label: corpus-correlation
mem_fence.memclass.note: NOT PROMOTED, same reason as mem_fence.sub: no ordering observable.
mem_fence.memclass.semantics: INERT with respect to the carrier's output: all 256 values pass.

mem_fence.sub.label: corpus-correlation
mem_fence.sub.note: NOT PROMOTED. This carrier has no memory-ORDERING observable (a single 8-lane threadgroup with a trailing barrier), so a pass bounds acceptance and dataflow inertness only, not the fence's semantics. Recorded so nobody re-probes it blindly.
mem_fence.sub.semantics: 192 of 256 values leave the carrier's functional output correct.

tg_addr_compute.b3.note: M4 confirmation of EXP-M4-14's A18 result (5 values there, 256 here).
tg_addr_compute.b3.semantics: INERT on M4: all 256 values leave the tile dataflow exact.

tg_addr_compute.b4.semantics: INERT on M4: all 256 values pass.

tg_addr_compute.b5.label: hardware-run
tg_addr_compute.b5.semantics: INERT on M4: all 256 values pass.

threadgroup_barrier.b5.label: hardware-run
threadgroup_barrier.b5.semantics: INERT: all 256 values leave the litmus exact.

threadgroup_barrier.flags.label: hardware-run
threadgroup_barrier.flags.note: Was `corpus-correlation` (0x09 tg/none, 0x08 device, 0x0e texture). The litmus is proven fence-sensitive by its own falsifier (224/256 lanes read stale zeros when the barrier is neutralised), so this is a real negative, not an insensitive carrier.
threadgroup_barrier.flags.semantics: INERT with respect to the fence: all 256 values leave the 256-lane litmus exact.

threadgroup_barrier.mem_scope.label: hardware-run
threadgroup_barrier.mem_scope.note: Dense confirmation of EXP-0093's 'byte+3 bit0 is the EXECUTION-CONVERGENCE enable, independent of the requested memory-fence class', now over all 256 values.
threadgroup_barrier.mem_scope.semantics: Only BIT 0 matters for a threadgroup-memory litmus: all 128 odd values pass and all 128 even values fail with 224/256 lanes reading stale zeros. The memory-CLASS bits are don't-care here; bit 0 is the execution-convergence enable.

threadgroup_barrier.sub.label: hardware-run
threadgroup_barrier.sub.semantics: Machine-derived exact rule `v & 0x06 == 0x04`: bit 2 must be 1 and bit 1 must be 0; bit 0 and bits 3..7 are DON'T CARE (64 of 256 values work, the compiler's own 0x04 and its 0x05 neighbour among them).
